versions.name: RXV2-0.9.758-sim-roles-clear
versions.notes: Making the two simulator routes plain (Malcolm 2026-09-18: 'a receiver with transceivers should STILL be able to operate in Simulator mode! It's even simpler for use as a receiver is built in'). He is quite right, and it always could - the receiver's own Simulator mode was never touched by yesterday's new role and needs no wire and no second board: a receiver plugs straight into the computer and flies the simulator from your own transmitter. What was wrong was the dongle page, which offered a board with its own radio the wire-fed Simulator interface role and then refused it. That option is now simply not offered to a board with transceivers, and the page says where its own Simulator mode lives instead. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.757-simulator-interface
versions.notes: The dongle gains a third role: Simulator interface (Malcolm 2026-09-17: 'all we need to do is add to the dongle a new option called Simulator interface'). A board with no radio, with one of your receivers wired to it, becomes a USB joystick for a simulator on the computer - Windows or Mac. Wiring is the same four-wire lead with the flight-controller end moved to the receiver: the receiver's signal output to D5, its 5 V to the board's 5V pin, ground to ground; then a USB cable to the computer, which powers the whole rig. No battery, no flight controller. CRSF, SBUS, IBUS and PPM are recognised on their own, and the Mode card says which was found and how many channels arrived. Everything else - which stick drives which axis, reversing, the spool-up realism, the camera keys - is on the Simulator pages exactly as it has always been, because the decoded channels are put precisely where the radio would have put them. This retires the separate LDRC2SIM firmware: one board, one firmware, three roles. A board with transceivers fitted is refused this role, because it belongs in a helicopter. Nothing changes for a receiver or a Rotorflight dongle.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.756-preflight-review
versions.notes: Pre-flight review of every firmware change since the last flown build (0.9.728), the night before Malcolm's next test flight. Verdict: nothing in that diff can touch control in the air - every changed path runs on the ground and is gated off when armed or under a live transmitter link. It found three things worth fixing anyway. 1) The tail-waggle fix from 0.9.729 never worked in the real landing order: the rotor-speed sample sat inside a block that only runs after the safety switch, by which time the motor already reads zero, so the 20-second coast wait never engaged and the tail still waggled on a turning head. The rotor is now watched every tick - one comparison. 2) The stall that switches the radios off after arming waited up to 1.5 s for the transmitter to acknowledge its warning; a transmitter busy with its safety-switch sound could push that stall to over two seconds after the arm switch, into the spool-up for a pilot quick on the motor switch. That wait is now capped at half a second, so the stall lands within 0.8 s - close to the +0.3 s every flight so far has flown with. 3) The 20-second WiFi hold after a Bluetooth update never held: its timer was compared unsigned against a time in the future and wrapped, so the join started 200 ms after boot as before. Also: the new bank-count setting is now refused under a live transmitter link, like every other setting saved to flash. Firmware only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.755-release-script
versions.notes: One command now does a whole release (Malcolm 2026-09-17: fourteen releases in a day, every one by hand - 'by all means do it now'). dev/release.sh bumps the version, prepends these notes, bumps the page asset versions, rebuilds the search index, runs every publish gate, builds the firmware and the filesystem and refuses a partial image, copies the images to both release trees, bumps and publishes the Android app (which syncs the app webroots), stages and publishes to messiter.com and checks the live manifest, bumps, builds and installs the iOS app on both devices, restarts the fleet watcher, commits, pushes and pings the watch - stopping hard at the first thing that fails. The fleet watcher now lives in the repository too (it had been in a session scratchpad, where it would have vanished), and pings by ntfy, the channel that actually reaches the watch. Nothing changes on the receiver itself.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.754-modal-scroll
versions.notes: A message box taller than the screen now scrolls inside itself, with its title and buttons staying put - What's in the backup lists forty-odd lines and ran off the bottom with no way to reach OK (Malcolm 2026-09-17). Applies to every message box. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.753-heal-timing
versions.notes: The 0.9.752 USB heal fired both its stages one millisecond apart (RAW420AJB log: 'sent exit' at 51.334 s, 'closed' at 51.335 s), so the flight controller never got the two or three seconds it needs to restart after 'exit'. Both stages were timed from the moment the port opened and gated on the same byte count, which was not reached until 51 s - then both passed at once. Stage 2 now waits 8 seconds after stage 1, and the byte gate is a dozen probes rather than forty. Firmware only; nothing changes in the air.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.752-cli-left-open
versions.notes: The deaf USB of 0.9.751 explained, and cured at the root. The receiver's own log from before that reboot showed it: 'Rotorflight command line open over USB' 21 seconds after the app connected, then every backup read REFUSED ('the command line is open - save or exit it first'), then the firmware install and reboot - with the flight controller still sitting in its command line, where it ignores MSP entirely. Three fixes. 1) Before every reboot the receiver now leaves the command line properly ('exit', no save - exactly as the Leave button does), instead of merely forgetting it had one open. 2) If a page asks for MSP while the command line has been open and untouched for 10 seconds, the receiver leaves it for you and says so - a page asking is the pilot having moved on, and Malcolm's own words are 'I frequently forget to press exit'. Before this a whole backup could be refused read by read without anyone noticing. 3) The heal from 0.9.751 now sends 'exit' first when a freshly-plugged flight controller stays silent, which restarts one that was left in its command line by an older receiver or a power-cut, and only then falls back to the receiver lead with the power-cycle advice. Nothing changes in the air: every one of these runs on the ground with the transmitter off.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.751-deaf-usb
versions.notes: Straight after a Bluetooth firmware update the Rotorflight page said 'No flight controller answering - check it is powered, its port, or the USB cable' (Malcolm 2026-09-17). The cable was fine. The flight controller's USB had come back from the restart enumerated but deaf: it answered none of 245 probes. The receiver already closes the USB link before every reboot, which is usually enough; this time it was not, and this chip has no way to cycle the USB power itself. So the receiver now notices - open for 8 s, plenty sent, not one answer - drops the dead port so Rotorflight goes over the receiver lead (or a dongle's UART) instead, logs what it did, and the pages say the one true thing: power the model off and on to bring USB back. Nothing changes in the air.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.750-whats-in-backup
versions.notes: A backup can now be read by a person. Backup & restore has a new button, What's in the backup, which folds everything the phone holds into plain lines - 'PIDs - banks 1-6', 'Rates - banks 1-6', 'Servos - 4', and so on - with the item count and when it was taken (Malcolm 2026-09-17, having opened the exported file: 'it means little to a mere human'). Both apps now name every item they hold; the page does the folding. Pages and apps only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.749-offers-in-turn
versions.notes: The app's own update and the receiver's firmware update were both offered on one screen (Malcolm 2026-09-17: 'I coped - but in sequence would be better'). Now the front page holds its firmware offer while the app's update dialog is up, so they come one at a time: app first, because updating the app restarts it, and the firmware offer comes back by itself on reconnect. A plain browser has no app dialog and is unaffected. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.748-page-load-order
versions.notes: Seven tuning pages have been dead since 0.9.742 this morning - PIDs, PID +, Rates, Governor (profile), Rescue, Easy tuning and Copy a bank: no bank buttons, no Save, nothing (Malcolm 2026-09-17: 'the copy from and the copy to boxes are both empty!', on Android and iPhone alike). One mistake, made seven times: app.js is loaded 'deferred', which means it runs AFTER a page's own script, and the six-bank change put a call into app.js at the very top of each page's script - so the page's whole script died before it defined anything. Every one is fixed by doing that work when the page has finished loading instead. The same fault was found lying in wait on the Fly page, where the status card had sat at '...' for ever, so that is fixed too. And a new gate now runs each page's script exactly as the browser does, before app.js exists, and refuses to publish anything that breaks - it caught all eight. Pages only; nothing changes in the air.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.747-ride-out-drops
versions.notes: Malcolm's 'crash' was not a crash (2026-09-17): 'the app returned to the opening screen, but the model wasn't selectable'. The Bluetooth link had dropped mid-session, and both apps treated any drop outside a reboot they had asked for as 'the model was switched off' and went straight to the scanner - with auto-connect disarmed, while the receiver was still tearing the old link down, so a tap on the model went nowhere. Now any unexpected drop from a live link is ridden out: 30 seconds of quiet reconnecting (90 for a reboot the app asked for), and if that window closes the scanner opens with auto-connect ARMED, so the receiver connects by itself the moment it is seen again. A model that really was switched off still lands on the scanner promptly. The receiver now logs WHY a link dropped (the radio's own reason code: lost each other, the phone ended it, we ended it), so the next one is diagnosable from the log alone. Firmware change is that one log line; nothing changes in the air.

rotorflight.line: Rotorflight 2.3 — the release these pages are written and tested against.
